t: In a federation a constitution divides power between a central government and member states, each governing its citizens directly in its own fields; neither can abolish the other.
It differs from a confederation, a league of sovereign states whose common council acts through them, and from a unitary state, whose regions hold only the powers the centre grants.
Pioneered by the United States in 1789 and adopted by Switzerland, Canada, Germany, Australia and India, federations are now home to about 40 per cent of the world’s people.
dyk: Switzerland is still officially the Swiss Confederation, Confoederatio Helvetica in Latin, the source of its abbreviation CH, although it has been a federal state rather than a confederation since its constitution of 1848.
ev: The Constitution of the United States takes effect, turning a confederation into the first modern federation
After the Sonderbund War, Switzerland’s new constitution turns its confederacy into a federal state
Seceding southern states form the Confederate States of America, and the American Civil War begins
The British North America Act unites three colonies in the federal Dominion of Canada
The German Empire is founded as a federation of 25 states under the king of Prussia
After referendums in each colony, six Australian colonies federate as the Commonwealth of Australia
India’s constitution comes into force, making the country a “Union of States”
The Soviet Union, a federation of fifteen union republics, is dissolved

f.power: Divided by the constitution between a federal government and the governments of the member states, each supreme in its own fields
f.legitimacy: A written constitution, usually a compact of the member states or their peoples, that neither level of government can change alone
f.chosen: Each level has its own elected government; the member states are usually represented in an upper house of the federal parliament, such as a senate or federal council
f.examples: the United States (since 1789), the Swiss Confederation (since 1848), the Dominion of Canada (since 1867), the German Empire (1871–1918), the Commonwealth of Australia (since 1901), the Republic of India (since 1950)
